newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ DLR ENDS OFF LOWS AFTER HITTING 29-MONTH TROUGH.
newsitem.headline: NZ DLR ENDS OFF LOWS AFTER HITTING 29-MONTH TROUGH.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed off its lows after it fell to a fresh 29-month low on Friday.
Dealers said the weak Australian dollar continued to weigh on the kiwi, which at US$0.6346 was at its lowest level since early March, 1995.
It ended at 0.6354/61 from its 0.6373/80 opening.
"It's probably going to struggle now to get back up through 0.6380. I think we'll have a look at 0.6330 in the next day or two," the dealer said.
Dealers said the kiwi suffered as players with weak positions cut out, but it was approaching a base. A 0.6335-90 band is forecast early next week.
"It's not a screaming sell like it has been in the last few days," said an Auckland bank dealer.
The kiwi has fallen eight cents, or 11 percent against the greenback, since November last year.
The Trade-Weighted Index closed at 64.14, its lowest level for over a year, and down from its 64.41 opening.

Short-term wholesale interest rates have risen to offset the kiwi's recent sharp decline and keep monetary conditions from straying too far from the RBNZ's comfort zone -- a 50 point band around its desired level. However, the Monetary Conditions Index eased to over 100 points beyond the bank's desired level prompted fears of a comment or intervention from the bank.
The central bank has twice warned markets in the past month that conditions were too loose.
With the New Zealand economy struggling to emerge from its trough, many believe the RBNZ should sanction looser conditions to allow rates to fall and growth to pick up.
Dealers said the longer the bank refrained from commenting the more the market would read that as sanctioning easier conditions.
